title: Rescuing the Foolish General: Accidentally Reversing the Odds to Become a Pampered Empress
author: Ling Lingling
synopsis: Modern illustrator Ye Li time-travels into the body of a mute girl, possessing nothing but her beauty. What? Even her beauty is self-proclaimed? This world doesn't love beauties, it loves chubby girls? Misfortunes never come singly, right after crossing over, she is bestowed in marriage to a disabled general. Very well, time to play the romance trope; when it comes to palace intrigue, she absolutely refuses to lose! Focusing wholeheartedly on her career, she becomes a saint of painting, accidentally researches culinary arts and opens restaurants everywhere, and even sells milk tea in ancient times to make a fortune, funding the general's army. But why is her own husband, a world-renowned general, actually a PTSD sufferer who tries to commit suicide day in and day out? What is he trying to do? Lin Daiyu isn't popular here, hello! And he comes with a dual...

chapters.title: Cause and Effect, Arrow of Destiny
chapters.content:
So warm.

Waking up from the darkness, Ye Li found herself being held by a stranger, lying in his arms.

A masculine scent mixed with a pungent smell of blood, along with a dull ache, reminded her...

She had transmigrated.

And she was injured along with the man in front of her.

An arrow had strung the two of them together, and they lay in an intimate posture while doctors nearby frantically tried to treat them, struggling to separate them.

Her mind suddenly grew dizzy...

A long flood of unfamiliar memories followed one after another, and she miserably discovered that she had transmigrated into an ancient mute girl.

A quarter of an hour ago, this mute girl and a man were being assassinated in the middle of the street.

The chaotic and noisy sounds of the street, fleeing civilians panicking, war-torn turmoil.

To carry out an assassination in the most prosperous part of the capital, the assassins were truly ferocious, and their methods were ruthless enough!

The man struck by the arrow at the same time held Ye Li with one arm while dodging and fighting back, carefully protecting her.

However, because they were pierced together by the sharp arrow, their bodies were forced close, making movement extremely inconvenient.

Amidst the alternating cries of "Guard the sovereign" and "Protect the general."

Reinforcements arrived, and the assassins retreated swiftly, unwilling to linger in battle.

In a flash, they vanished completely, leaving behind a scene of utter devastation.

Ye Li and the man she had just met were rescued by reinforcements and sent to the nearest inn. Because they were connected by the arrow, they had to lie in bed together, their bodies still pressed against one another, as a doctor used a knife to pull out the arrow...

The assassins had put their full ten percent strength into the arrow, and Ye Li was rudely awakened by wave after wave of excruciating pain...

Opening her eyes, she saw a quaint room with luxurious furnishings.

Everything was different from the modern world.

Beside her, the sound of "ying ying ying..." weeping endlessly echoed, as miserable as a funeral chant.

...

Starting off with Cupid's arrow right out of the gate? Truly the most fantastical transmigrator in history...

She wanted to ask where she was, but unfortunately she could only make the sound of "Ah... ah-ah-ah..."

From her angle, what she saw the most was the man's broad chest. Perhaps because the doctor's arrow-removal technique was too poor, she could see the other's chest heaving in spasms, as if enduring with all his might.

But Ye Li simply couldn't hold it in.

Tears overflowed, endless and continuous, sobbing and whimpering a few times like the bewildered and helpless sound of a small animal, making anyone who heard it feel an involuntary pang of heartache.

The doctor probably couldn't bear it either, and with a burst of effort, they were finally separated, and the arrow was pulled out...

Immediately, several people came over to bandage her and the man respectively.

The ying-ying-ying sound next to them cried even louder, wailing pitifully:

"General... General, you must not have any mishaps!"

"The Beichen Kingdom harbors wild ambitions, and this time they must be the ones behind it; you must hold on... ying ying ying."

This woman wept bitterly, yet noisily.

After the initial pain passed, Ye Li now calmed down, lying down to sort out the situation:

The original body she had transmigrated into was originally a mute girl living in an alternate-history dynasty.

The original owner's parents were a young couple who sold sugar paintings, and she had an older brother. Their life was ordinary and peaceful, and the only skill she could show off was that her sugar paintings were passable.

In this point, she shared a common trait with Ye Li, who had been an illustrator before transmigrating.

Today was the original owner's birthday, and her older brother had taken her out to a tavern, wanting to buy a roasted chicken as a birthday gift for her.

As a result, halfway there, they ran into a large-scale offensive by assassins targeting the general, and Ye Li got separated from her brother in the chaos.

Then came the moment when the assassins found her blocking the way, and just as the blade was raised and brought down...

She was caught in a broad embrace and pulled away to safety; a general in grey-blue robes had saved her.

This general bore the sword wound himself while trying his utmost to protect the original owner, an ordinary citizen. He shielded her behind his back until arrows coming from all directions turned them into a hedgehog...

The original owner was gone, and she had arrived.

Listening to the crying female voice, it seemed the general was severely injured.

Thinking about how this person had saved a total stranger among the common people, he must be a kind-hearted person.

And he was a general too, protecting his home and country, so righteous and imposing!

Ye Li raised her eyes, staring wide-eyed...

She discovered that this general had clear eyebrows and bright eyes, the noble bearing of a dragon hidden and a phoenix soaring, truly carrying a dashing and heroic appearance.

Even splashed with the ink-like stains of blood, his poise remained undiminished.

They say appearance stems from the heart; such a graceful and handsome young man possessed a kind heart as well, good people truly get rewarded.

"Who on earth dares to be so audacious! Assassinating someone in the capital is an unforgivable crime!"

The newcomer wore a fully embroidered yellow robe, his hair crown inlaid with gold and jade. His bearing was dashing, truly the epitome of wealth and luxury.

He walked straight in and was stunned upon seeing the two injured people lying on the bed...

"What... is going on here?"

Immediately, someone stepped forward to explain to the man in yellow:

"Rusheng pays respects to Your Majesty. Assassins were slaughtering civilians randomly, and the general saved this woman."

"However, the assassins pierced both their bodies with arrows, so they could only be carried back together..."

The speaker's voice was clear and pure, sounding quite young, also dressed in blue robes.

He paused, looked nervously at the general, and then said with worry:

"The general has suffered multiple arrow wounds; old injuries have not healed while new ones are added. Please forgive Your Majesty for failing to attend the imperial summons on time."

The Emperor said, "These are minor matters now. How is the general?"

The doctor replied tremblingly:

"Both injured parties have lost too much blood, and furthermore, there is poison on this arrow... I'm afraid..."

The Emperor grew anxious and urged, "Afraid of what? Speak directly!"

The doctor answered with fear and trepidation:

"I'm afraid his martial arts will not be what they used to be, and holding a sword..."

"...will be rather strenuous."

This was already a euphemistic answer; he might be crippled, but he didn't dare say it directly.

Upon hearing this, the Emperor fell silent.

Instead, the man in blue, Rusheng, exclaimed, "What did you say? How could that happen to the general?!"

That ying-ying-ying female voice cried out even louder:

"I beg you, I beg you, please save Lord General! He cannot be allowed to have any mishaps... ying ying ying..."

The Emperor seemed to notice the weeping woman only then, and said in a deep voice:

"Wanning? Why are you here?"

The weeping woman named Wanning acted as if she had suffered some grave injury, swaying as she said:

"Next month is my father's birthday, and this humble commoner went out to look at inkstones, but witnessed the general being assassinated... ying ying ying..."

Seeing a beauty shed tears, the Emperor comforted Wanning while promising to send the finest inkstones from the palace tomorrow.

Such a picture of mutual affection between a man and a woman.

On this side, the man in blue, Rusheng, kept tending to the heavily wounded general.

Ever since she obtained the original owner's memories and knew that the person before her had saved her, Ye Li had also been worried about his injuries.

However, the general kept his eyes closed from beginning to end and didn't utter a single word.

Ye Li recalled that after the assassins left, the original owner's last memory was of the general finally unable to hold back, coughing up a mouthful of blood that accidentally splashed onto her.

Before the original owner fainted, the last thing she heard was his voice: "I'm sorry for implicating you, young lady..."

After the doctor finished treating the wounds, the man in blue continued to instruct:

"Be sure to use the best medicine, and treat this young girl well too so she can recover as soon as possible."

Ye Li couldn't help sighing with emotion; the man in blue, Rusheng, was probably the only one in the whole room who genuinely wished for the two of them to get better.

Before she could indulge in much more sentiment, however, the Emperor began issuing decrees:

"Move them to another room; the smell of blood here is too heavy."

"Wait..." Wanning suddenly softly persuaded the man in yellow:

"Having suffered such heavy injuries, it might be better to just separate them with a curtain and not move the wounds for now."

Her words were earnest, and the Emperor nodded in agreement.

Unexpectedly, however, the Emperor dropped a bombshell the very next second:

"In a moment, I will bestow a marriage upon them."

...

Getting married right after transmigrating?

Ye Li angrily protested in her heart!

She waved her hands vigorously, but was ignored.

Wanning looked slightly flustered at this moment. She hurried forward a few steps and spoke:

"Your Majesty is benevolent, but a matter of marriage after all still needs..."

The Emperor's tone shifted as he grasped her hand with irresistible firmness, saying:

"Wanning, I know the engagement between the two of you was annulled long ago. Now that Mo Chen has had intimate physical contact with this woman, if I don't bestow a marriage..."

The Emperor's gaze was like a hook, chilling Ye Li to the bone.

"I'm afraid both of their reputations will be ruined!"

...

Oh ho, how high-sounding he makes it.

Listening to their conversation, Wanning was this man's former fiancée.

The Emperor himself was holding the weeping woman's little hand on one side, while forcibly bestowing a marriage between a dignified general and herself, a mute, on the other...

Who knows what he was plotting.

The Emperor merely glanced briefly at Ye Li, and seeing her ordinary attire, he generously waved a hand:

"When she is married off, let it be from the imperial-bestowed residence. Consider it a reward for her meritorious service in blocking the arrow."

Following that, the crowd departed in a grand commotion behind the Emperor.

Leaving Ye Li all alone, dumbfounded.

Me? I've just been bestowed a marriage like this?

Looking at the modeled face born for drawing before her, General Husband = Free Sketching Male Model, she hesitated inwardly:

A husband dispatched and home-delivered free of shipping by the state...

What should she do?

chapters.title: Five Hundred Glances Before the Buddha, Forging a Bond in This Life
chapters.content:
The night curtain hung low, windless and cloudless.

Unable to sleep, Ye Li could only quietly ponder her next move.

Before transmigrating, Ye Li was an illustrator, a homebody, rather plump, living alone and keeping five cats, living a very content and pleasant life.

Having a sudden burst of inspiration at the time, she drew an illustration of the Gates of the Underworld. Feeling too exhausted from drawing to move, she fell asleep right at her drafting table.

When she woke up, she had already arrived in this place.

They say strange things happen at the intersection of dusk.

Indeed, one should always listen to the elders...

She sighed silently, yet without self-pity.

Since childhood, she had a rather carefree disposition and could adapt to anywhere as quickly as possible.

Now...

She turned her head to look beside her; this newly acquired husband had already been cleaned up.

Behold a beauty beneath the moonlight, the more you look, the more delighted you become.

With star-like brows and sword-like eyes, and a superior bone structure, he was as standard as a sculpted plaster cast. Moreover, when he rescued her today, his body was full of strength, reminding her of the well-defined muscles of the David sculpture in the fine arts academy.

If it were this person, it actually wasn't that hard to accept.

After all, he was her savior.

Along the way, despite suffering such heavy injuries, he hadn't whimpered or cried out in pain. Transposed to modern times, marrying a soldier would make her a military wife. Yes, righteous and awe-inspiring, still pretty good.

"Creak."

In the middle of the night, the sound of a wooden door opening came through, exceptionally distinct.

Ye Li immediately grew tense. Who could it be this late?

She saw the man in blue from the daytime enter the room, and then he knelt straight down:

"General, the assassins were death squads sent by another country. But for them to know the General's whereabouts, I'm afraid someone was coordinating from the inside."

The man in blue paused.

"This woman's identity has also been verified. She is the daughter of a merchant; she could speak as a child but was later poisoned mute. She is indeed a law-abiding citizen, and her ancestors for three generations have been farmers with nothing suspicious."

"Mm. How are my injuries?"

The man lying on the bed still kept his eyes closed, as if fast asleep. But once the man in blue finished reporting, his cold, detached voice asked faintly.

This gave Ye Li quite a shock...

What? You weren't actually passed out today?!

With acting skills this good, why aren't you an Oscar winner?!

"The doctor says..." The man in blue's throat suddenly choked up, and he answered with difficulty:

"I... fear you need to recuperate quietly for some time... General, rest assured! I will find Divine Divine Doctor Mu as soon as possible! I will definitely restore the General to how you were before..."

"There is poison on the arrows; their purpose goes beyond this." The young general's voice was utterly flat. After a moment, he slowly said:

"This hand of mine... I'm afraid it's ruined..."

The man in blue said in horror, "This subordinate will definitely find Divine Divine Doctor Mu..."

The general pressed his lips together and calmly interrupted him:

"Rufang, help me send a letter of safety to this girl's family. She was innocently implicated and suffered because of me. Bring more silver."

Hearing this, the subordinate named Rufang bowed respectfully toward Ye Li. As the most capable assistant, Rufang was completely obedient to his general. Receiving the order, he hurried off.

Coming in haste, leaving in a rush.

Leaving behind a room of tranquility.

Ye Li had thought this general would say something to her.

She hadn't expected that after his subordinate Rufang left, he wouldn't make a sound again.

...

Hey, hey, hey, you can't be like this.

We're really getting married by imperial decree just like that, huh?

They were now lying on the same large bed, separated only by a thin layer of gauze.

Ye Li had originally intended to lift this layer of gauze; even if she couldn't speak, at least she could write a bit or draw to communicate.

A young man of literature and art would never be defeated by such a minor obstacle before her!

To her surprise, before she could make a move, the thin gauze had already been lifted.

The young general finally cast his gaze over. He looked at Ye Li with emotions impossible to untangle in his eyes, his voice low:

"It has implicated you, Miss... Apologies..."

Hearing this, all the sorrow and grievance Ye Li had accumulated throughout the day suddenly collapsed.

Tears blurred her vision...

The young general's face, emitting a soft glow under the moonlight, seemed to pause, likely because seeing a woman shed tears at such close range left him at a loss.

Having remained silent all evening, he stammered out an apology:

"This subordinate offers his sincere apologies. Pressing circumstances compelled me to offend you; this is entirely Mo Chen's fault."

He paused. "Later on, Miss and I were both wounded by sharp arrows; this is Mo Chen's second fault."

At this moment, Ye Li streamed with tears, as quiet as a frightened little animal.

Quiet and well-behaved; this was Mo Chen's first impression of Ye Li.

"The Emperor resolved to bestow a marriage, needlessly dragging Miss into this. This is Mo Chen's third fault."

The young general's expression was dim, his voice lacking its previous chill as he said with bitterness:

"The matter of the bestowed marriage is a foregone conclusion, but I am injured and poisoned, and my days are numbered..."

"Miss can simply treat this as changing to a temporary residence elsewhere. Our marital bond will naturally be annulled upon my death. Thereafter, all the wealth of the General's estate shall belong entirely to Miss, and with your purity intact, you may remarry."

Mo Chen's injuries were extremely severe, and coupled with speaking so much, he was coughing by the end of it.

Hearing him speak this way, as if arranging his final affairs, Ye Li felt a wave of sympathy.

The one who was injured wasn't me, it was the original owner. Since you've already sent a letter of safety to the original owner's family, it shows you have a heart.

She reached out her hand and gently pressed it against Mo Chen's chest, slowly smoothing his breath for him.

Mo Chen had spent long years on the battlefield, rarely interacting with women, and this was his first time sharing a bed with one. Ye Li's such-bold action made him cough even harder...

????

Ye Li thought: Is he really this shy?!!...

The intermittent coughs in the dark night, even though deliberately suppressed by their owner, were exceptionally distinct.

Ye Li struggled to sit up, poured a cup of water by the bedside, and supported Mo Chen as he drank it down.

Gradually, the young man's cough subsided...

Seeing his ears red like carrots, Ye Li thought it was rather cute.

After Mo Chen calmed down, he collected his thoughts.

Knowing his time was short, as if needing to settle all matters completely, he said with pity:

"Mo Chen knows he has failed Miss, but I still earnestly request Miss to grant my sole plea."

"There are many in the General's estate who contracted lingering illnesses on the battlefield. Previously, the estate's private treasury provided them some relief. I hope that after Miss takes charge of the household management... cough cough... do not cut off this supply..."

He seemed to want to arrange everything properly.

Ye Li felt she still needed to try communicating.

She made "mm-mm" sounds and used hand gestures to remind him to reach out his hand.

Then she took the General's wrist, unfolded his palm, and began writing on it.

Stroke by stroke, she wrote very slowly, but very earnestly.

"My name is Ye Li."

Ye Li told him her name. After a day of getting along, she felt this young general had a clear train of thought and a kind nature, so she decided to make a friend of him.

The crucial point was that having transacted here, he was the only person she knew!

"Miss Ye, please forgive the offense. I am Mo Chen."

After a brief ponder, Ye Li decided to straighten out their attitudes with him; a blind marriage and a mute match was no good.

She wrote again: "I don't care about chastity and purity. Are you willing to marry? If not, I can call off the wedding."

Mo Chen was slightly surprised by Ye Li's act of defying the imperial decree, likely assuming Ye Li already had someone in her heart and therefore was unwilling to accept the bestowed marriage.

"I'm afraid... I cannot grant Miss's wish," Mo Chen sighed, his lowered eyes full of helplessness.

Ye Li sighed inwardly, writing carefully:

"I am merely a commoner with a physical disability; I cannot be considered a good wife."

Seeing that her reason was not because she had someone else in her heart, but rather self-deprecation due to her mute affliction, Mo Chen pressed his lips together and said patiently:

"Though I am a General, I am also about to become a cripple and can barely protect myself... In this matter, I am afraid I lack the power to resist the decree."

Ye Li watched dramas; whenever court intrigue was involved, a single misstep meant total ruin.

Though she didn't know why he had to fake fainting during the day, the two of them were still unfamiliar now, and she didn't know if it was appropriate to ask about such confidential matters.

"The reason I stood pat today was to see what the people behind the scenes are really up to. Only thus can we lure the enemy into laxity."

Mo Chen immediately and proactively cleared up her confusion.

Well, not bad. No communication barriers.

With this general's clear logic and ability to bide his time, based solely on the few words exchanged in the palm of his hand, Ye Li wanted to exclaim:

Splendid!

He really was a fascinating person.

Clearly hunted down and targeted, yet possessing deep compassion, he had saved a mute.

With the situation unfavorable, he stood pat and prepared for the worst.

Even facing a completely defenseless mute girl, he patiently explained his affairs rather than putting on airs of mystery.

In ancient times, distinctions of status were strict; for a man to show such humility toward inferiors was truly rare.

Ye Li had arrived in this world for the first time amidst swords and bloodshed.

A sudden burst of gentleness shattered a certain unwarranted fortitude.

Ye Li pondered for a moment, raised her hand, and wrote:

"I am willing to marry you."

Simple and direct.

Without reservation.

Perhaps because no woman had ever been so straightforward before, it was obvious that the young general before her lost his prior composure, his hand trembling slightly for a fleeting moment.

Although he tried to appear normal, in the dark night without sight, the tactile sensation in their palms grew increasingly pronounced, and Ye Li felt the temperature rise considerably.

It was... rather cute.

A tingling sensation washed over, like a butterfly skimming across the lake of her heart, stirring ripples.

"Cough cough... Mhm... This matter, after all, has implicated Miss..."

Then Mo Chen fell silent again.

Probably from shyness, he wasn't as aloof as he had been in the daytime, nor as calm as when assigning tasks to his subordinates.

Ye Li saw a side of him hidden from outsiders, pure, shy, and gentle.

"Then, have you ever liked any other girl?"

The young general paused, his voice filled with bitterness as he said wistfully:

"In my youth, my family arranged a betrothal in the womb with a young lady."

"The woman from daytime? You liked her very much?"

"The elders arranged the engagement before I was born; I only saw her a few times when I was little..."

"Later, my life hung in the balance on the battlefield. Her family thought I had died a martyr, so they betrothed her to someone else, but before she was married, her new husband's family suffered an accidental death..."

"I only learned of these past events after returning from the battlefield."

Ye Li felt she might have asked too much. He had shed blood on the battlefield and was even presumed dead.

How tragic that must have been...

Returning after a narrow escape with death, how could one open up old scars?

She wrote on his hand:

"I'm sorry. I just wanted to understand you better."

Ye Li hardly dared to raise her head to look at his expression, writing quickly to explain herself as soon as possible.

"I have never been betrothed, nor have I ever liked anyone else. You are the only person I will marry."

Stroke by stroke, spreading from the palm into the blood, and then into the heart.

It was hard to describe the feeling.

Mo Chen knew himself never to be one to indulge in mortal entanglements.

He was busy with warfare and obsessed with swordsmanship.

He had never had such an opportunity, nor such a person, who dared to ask about his private matters, nor had he ever talked about the past like this.

Yet never did he expect that in this life, he would let down his guard before a woman who could not speak.

From the moment they met, this woman had been implicated and injured, yet had never uttered a single word.

Mo Chen had felt her pulse; this woman possessed no martial arts, and when pain from her injuries struck, she merely shed tears in silence.

Being forcibly arranged for treatment, shared a bed, and even bestowed a marriage, she neither made a fuss nor caused trouble; rather, she carefully devised solutions, handling advance and retreat with propriety.

Moreover, compared to the sheltered ladies of noble households, though she came from common folk, she possessed her own insight and bearing.

Her simple and direct manner of doing things felt far more refreshing than roundabout twists and turns.

He watched as Ye Li wrote in his palm:

"Since our marriage is an accomplished fact, I hope we can live in peace hereafter."

"Once the storm passes and the time is right, give me a letter of separation."

Perhaps because she had just said "you are the only person I will marry," seeing the words "letter of separation" brought a trace of unease to the bottom of Mo Chen's heart.

He responded in a timely manner:

"You will also be the only wife of Mo Chen in this life."

He said solemnly.

A slightly magnetic voice lingered by her ear, carrying the young man's firm promise, and for an instant, Ye Li was dazed.

Clearly, the two of them were merely making a temporary pact regarding their future living situation.

Yet it felt like a lover's confession...

Ye Li's heart beat fast, her mind repeatedly echoing:

You will also be the only wife of Mo Chen in this life...You will be the only wife of my lifetime...The only wife in this life...This life...Only.

chapters.title: The Dashing Young Master Yields Financial Power
chapters.content:
"You are the only wife of my life."

This sentence echoed repeatedly in her mind.

Help, this is way too flirtatious!

An inexperienced singleton like me cannot handle this kind of stimulation!

Just as Ye Li was wondering how she should respond,

in the quiet night, a "rumble" suddenly sounded.

Ye Li's... stomach... growled...

"Rumble."

Another sound.

A fatal blow.

Having not eaten much due to her injuries, her stomach abruptly protested amidst the romantic atmosphere.

Never would she have expected, the awkwardness was broken by awkwardness itself!

I have no face left to show...

...

"I'm hungry."

Ye Li wrote, "Is there anything to eat?"

"Wait a moment."

Mo Chen called out softly toward the window:

"Rufeng, bring some food, and go fetch the box from the secret room."

Goodness gracious!

Ye Li didn't hear any echo from outside, nor did she see a shadow, but miraculously, before long, Rufeng entered with food.

Such lightness-of-foot martial arts, this is incredible!!!

If a subordinate is this capable, the general's martial arts must be even more remarkable!

It seems the most important thing right now is to tightly hug her future husband's thigh, get well-fed and warmly clothed, and the whole family will be worry-free.

Ye Li gained a deeper understanding of her survival goals.

While eating, she remembered that Mo Chen was injured, so she also served him some food.

The young general saw that she felt no disgust toward him, and his heart warmed.

The situation right now truly wasn't good, and he had been poisoned...

He looked at Ye Li, who was eating with great relish, and said:

"The Emperor has bestowed this marriage. From now on, you are the mistress of the General's Estate."

"I am poisoned now, and I might fall unconscious later. From now on, all matters big and small in the General's Estate are entrusted to you."

He looked at her, his gaze calm.

Ye Li was stunned. I just got here, and you already trust me?!

You're handing over such a huge General's Estate for me to manage?

Ye Li thought: While it's true that everyone has their uses, this is not how you use them!

Mo Chen took the box brought by Rufeng and opened it. It was filled to the brim with thick stacks of silver banknotes and gold ingots.

He handed all this money to Ye Li and said solemnly:

"Since you and I are now married, you should take charge of these for household management."

"As for the matter I entrusted to you previously, consider this your compensation. Thank you for your hard work..."

Ye Li somewhat dazedly took the thick stack of bills, and a huge wave surged in her heart!

Well, that's just fantastic!

Everyone has their uses.

And this is precisely my use!

Ye Li flashed a huge, brilliant smile at Mo Chen.

With this smile, Ye Li instantly radiated a breathtakingly amiable warmth.

It wasn't so much her dazzling beauty, but rather the genuine, tangible joy of receiving a huge fortune that made her smile super bright...

It could be said that her affection for the vulgar thing called money was displayed without any reservation.

Ye Li smiled and nodded, accepting it.

With this much money, if it's still not enough, I'll sell milk tea in ancient times to support you!

Looking at it this way, this unexpectedly acquired husband looked even better and more handsome!

Particularly pleasing to the eye!

Mo Chen and Rufeng talked for a while longer. Ye Li, standing nearby, had her mind drift far away and wasn't listening closely, leaving only a smile at the corner of her lips that seemed frozen, lingering for a long time.

Seeing her dazed appearance inadvertently, Mo Chen smiled unconsciously.

Rufeng wore a strange expression...

Weren't they just discussing military defense deployments? Why is the general not worried but instead smiling?

Ah, as expected of a general who plots strategies within a command tent!

He must have had a plan in mind long ago. Rufeng gazed at his general with an expression of admiration.

The general, silently worshipped by his subordinate, actually just felt that this woman was so genuine, far more genuine than anyone in the palace or the imperial court wearing masks.

People in the world call money dirt.

Among the scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants, merchants are the lowest because they carry the heaviest stench of copper, and worldly wisdom values not bowing for five buckets of rice.

Yet living in this world, who can truly live without money?

Looking at the person before him, whose eyes shone brightly at the sight of banknotes and whose smile at the corners of her mouth was uncontainable, set against a fair and pure face, Mo Chen felt that the woman before him was thoroughly real at this moment, devoid of pretentious hypocrisy, showing only the pure joy of receiving silver.

She really likes silver; Mo Chen concluded.

Time flew by. After the three finished discussing matters, Rufeng, whose whereabouts could not be exposed, had to leave shortly after the handover.

The next day, it was drizzling.

Suddenly, a few peals of thunder rattled the sky, waking Ye Li up.

She looked up, wanting to check on Mo Chen.

Only to find that Mo Chen's face was beet red; he seemed to have a fever!

Damn it! Having suffered such severe injuries, a fever was inevitable. In ancient times, there were no fever-reducing medications to take; recovery relied entirely on doctors and one's own immune system.

Disregarding her own pain, Ye Li got up, wanting to find a doctor, only to find the door locked and impossible to open no matter what. She tried opening the window, but that wouldn't budge either.

A completely sealed room.

Yesterday was an assassination; today is imprisonment in a locked room.

She walked over to the table, poured a cup of water, and gently propped Mo Chen up. At this moment, Mo Chen was in a hazy state of consciousness, as if walking through a desert, and obediently drank the water down.

Ye Li hurriedly finished and laid him back down. There was no help for it; her body had exerted every ounce of strength just to barely prop up an adult man, and feeding him water was already her limit.

Ye Li remembered that for a fever in ancient times, one could place a towel on the forehead for physical cooling.

She guarded him, taking care of him while waiting for his subordinate, Rufeng.

Suddenly, she heard a "click" outside the door. Ye Li rushed forward in a single bound and pulled the door open.

The door actually opened!

The door that was locked last night could finally be opened!

Ye Li looked outside and suddenly locked eyes with Rufeng.

Rufeng was obviously taken aback, presumably thinking Ye Li had misunderstood, and whispered an explanation:

"I had to leave last night, and I was afraid someone would come in and harm the injured general, so I locked it first. Though you couldn't go out, outsiders couldn't get in either. Please rest assured."

So that was it!

Goodness! You even thought of that.

Why didn't you just lock your general up every day!

After speaking, Rufeng even patted Ye Li's head reassuringly, then suddenly remembering her improper status, his expression turned stern, and he immediately apologized:

"Apologies, Milady. Subordinate just thought you looked like my sister and meant no offense."

Ye Li quickly grabbed Rufeng's wrist and pulled him over to Mo Chen.

Mo Chen's illness had worsened. Rufeng knelt down to inspect the wounds carefully, and with a solemn expression, said to Ye Li: "The poison in the general's body has begun to flare up. I must go immediately to fetch a doctor."

Rufeng spoke calmly to Ye Li:

"Milady, please hear me out! Although my general is not well-versed in romance, he is loyal, upright, and pure, a pillar of the nation. Now I must leave to find a medical remedy. I can only hope Milady will recall the general's past kindness in saving you and take good care of him."

With that, true to his name, Rufeng dashed away like the wind.

Leaving Ye Li alone to digest what had just been said.

Expecting a mute with no martial arts or medical skills to take care of a feverish patient.

It truly was desperate times calling for desperate measures. Fortunately, she was a time-traveler.

Ye Li was now accustomed to the various magical encounters brought by time travel, so she remained increasingly calm.

She figured taking care of a patient wasn't that difficult either.

Provided the patient stayed lying down without moving, allowing her to sketch a bit.

Suddenly, a sound of hammering and tapping came from outside, accompanied by messy, bustling footsteps and the shrill, ear-piercing voice of a eunuch. A group of people marched straight in, lining up consciously, holding gold, silver, jewelry, coral, and jade.

The head eunuch pinched his voice to proclaim:

"By the Emperor's decree, a marriage is specially bestowed upon the General. His Majesty is merciful and bestows a new imperial residence. Today, the wedding ceremony shall be held, and the marriage consummated this very day. Congratulations, congratulations!"

Ye Li waved her hand dismissively and pointed straight at Mo Chen's location, using gestures to indicate that he couldn't get up.

To her surprise, the eunuch offered a fake-smiling congratulation:

"His Majesty knows the General is gravely ill, and specially permits lying down for the wedding bows. The ceremony will be performed on your behalf by the Golden Phoenix."

Ye Li thought: "Golden Phoenix? Sounds like it's worth a lot."

The next second, a rooster wearing a gold necklace was held up by an attendant...

Ye Li: Forget it, let it all end...

~~~

chapters.title: Amnesia or Not, You Alone Remain Repeatedly in My Heart
chapters.content:
Ye Li knew they wanted her to bow in marriage with this rooster.

She muttered inwardly: Let it all end...

Pandora's box had nothing on this.

Regrettably, she was restrained by four matrons and taken to the new residence to change into wedding attire.

Once the servants had prepared everything, they escorted her to the wedding ceremony site in the new residence.

Ye Li couldn't catch her breath and almost died of anger.

There lay Mo Chen, dressed in bright red robes, the dazzling red contrasting against his ashen complexion.

That rooster stood rigidly right on his chest, occasionally bouncing and trampling his heart, could it get any more miserable?!

A dignified general, just because he was injured, could be humiliated like this?!

Utterly preposterous!

Too bad she couldn't speak, or she would have started cursing right then and there.

The eunuch's voice suddenly rang out: "Presenting the newlyweds to bow."

And then Ye Li was shoved forward to perform the bows.

After this purely humiliating ceremony concluded, they were escorted into the so-called bridal chamber.

The matchmaker pinched her voice, telling them to drink the nuptial wine, and hypocritically blessed them with an early birth of a son.

You try waking up this passed-out person first!

As for having children, am I supposed to have one by myself?

Ye Li could only helplessly act out the rest of this farce.

Once the eunuchs and palace maids finished their task, they swarmed out and left. Aside from the sea of red indicating the household's joyous occasion today, the atmosphere was desolate to the extreme.

Ye Li even saw someone secretly pocketing some of the gold and silver jewelry from the betrothal gifts.

What a declining age! When a tiger falls from the plains, it gets bullied by dogs!

Once the idle onlookers had all left, Ye Li hurriedly stripped off the obnoxious red garments from Mo Chen. She wouldn't have known if she hadn't undressed him, only to find that blood had seeped through the white undergarment beneath.

Splatters of blood and a web of wounds made for a truly horrifying sight.

He really had risked his all to save her back then.

Putting in a tremendous amount of effort, Ye Li rebandaged the wounds and helped him back onto the bed.

Now she just had to wait for Rufeng to bring the doctor back.

Suddenly her stomach began to growl "rumble rumble" again.

So Ye Li searched for the kitchen in this bestowed new residence and set about cooking.

Ingredients in ancient times were truly wonderful, natural and pollution-free.

Ye Li made pan-fried buns and sweet potato cakes, and cooked some congee for Mo Chen.

She tended to Mo Chen constantly, but unfortunately, he did not wake up.

Mo Chen ran a fever for three days before finally waking up.

At that time, Ye Li was feeding him some broth. Since he had been too weak to even eat congee earlier, she could only feed him liquids a little at a time.

She had just finished feeding him a bowl when she saw his fingers twitch, and then his eyes slowly fluttered open. Ye Li locked eyes with him, her heart overflowing with immense joy!

Mo Chen had finally woken up!

Yet the moment Mo Chen opened his eyes, they were filled with confusion and curiosity.

Unable to speak, Ye Li could only grab his hand and try to write characters on his palm.

Before she could even write, he grabbed her hand back, his voice hoarse and perplexed as he asked:

"Older Sister, who are you?"

Older Sister?

Ye Li was petrified on the spot!

"He actually called me older sister? What is going on?"

Could the poison he contracted have acted up?

At that moment, Rufeng was about to enter. Seeing that Mo Chen had awakened, he immediately rushed to the bedside.

Mo Chen saw Rufeng, and his bewildered expression turned into reassurance. He split his mouth open in a bright, cheerful smile:

"Brother Rufeng, you're here!"

Upon hearing "Brother Rufeng," Rufeng understood instantly, the general had indeed been plotted against and poisoned.

With a dark expression, he asked with heartache:

"How is Young Master feeling now? You had a fever earlier and remained unconscious for three full days without waking... Is anything still uncomfortable?"

Mo Chen pouted and said with his lips poked out:

"Me... I feel like I got beaten up by someone, I feel so tired everywhere, and my stomach is so empty. Wuwuwu, am I terminally ill? This is so uncomfortable..."

Rufeng said with heartache: "I'll have the Young Madam cook something delicious for you in a moment."

He pulled a candied hawthorn stick from his chest, carefully inspected it, and handed it to Mo Chen:

"Young Master, this is today's freshly made candied hawthorn. Not knowing which day you'd wake up, I went to buy one every day. You can eat it as soon as you finish your medicine."

"Wuwuwu, I don't want to drink medicine, I want to eat candy!" Hearing that he had to take medicine, Mo Chen actually started acting spoiled over a stick of candied hawthorn...

How bizarre!

Looking at Mo Chen right now, Ye Li thought he looked like a mentally impaired fool...

Gone was the composure and wisdom of the general of past days; he was just a foolish, bear-like child throwing a tantrum over candy, crying and making a fuss completely regardless of his image.

Mo Chen reached out and grabbed the candied hawthorn stick, biting off one piece right away, and mumbled while chewing: "Brother Rufeng, you're so nice. You buy my favorite candied hawthorn every day. Thank you, Brother Rufeng! I like you best."

The youth's clear voice overflowed with childlike innocence, making one can't help but smile.

Rufeng thought of how the usually stern general, once poisoned, would become frank, innocent, and speak his mind without reservation.

Yet his words were a bit too boldly straightforward, leaving Rufeng truly caught between laughter and tears.

Rufeng tried to take the candied hawthorn back, gently coaxing him: "Young Master has to drink his medicine first before eating candy."

Instead, he watched as Mo Chen licked every single candied hawthorn on the stick with his tongue before handing it back:

"They're all mine now, you can't eat them, okay? I've already marked them!"

Witnessing this divine operation, Ye Li was secretly shocked, no wonder he grew up to be a general.

Look at this move; isn't it just striking first to gain the upper hand from the thirty-six stratagems!

Rufeng took the candied hawthorn and solemnly promised: "Right, I won't eat them, I'll save them all for the Young Master."

Ye Li looked at this completely different Mo Chen, wearing a foolish grin with bits of candied hawthorn residue still stuck to the corner of his mouth.

Licking the candy while chatting with a somewhat smug little expression, she couldn't help but let out a soft laugh.

If a camera had recorded this, Mo Chen would probably cringe so hard upon seeing it later that he'd dig out a three-bedroom apartment with his toes...

Rufeng looked worried and apprehensive, but still managed to force a trace of gratification as he said: "Young Master Mo, as long as your health recovers, I'll buy as many as you want next time."

Mo Chen flashed a bright, crispy smile at him, exposing eight pearly white teeth, what a picture of an innocent, pure young master!

It practically blinded Ye Li's eyes, why did turning foolish make him even more vivid than his usual calm and restrained self?

Then Mo Chen's eyes rolled, and looking at Ye Li, who had been standing nearby the whole time, he asked very politely and earnestly:

"Brother Rufeng, may I ask who this pretty older sister is?"

???

What should a social-anxious illustrator do when her handsome husband gets poisoned and turns stupid!

Emergency!

Waiting online!

Rufeng looked at Ye Li and said to Mo Chen with slight tension:

"This is the Young Master's wife, the mistress of the General's Estate."

Upon hearing this, Mo Chen froze for a moment, then rolled his eyes around.

Unable to figure it out, he rolled his eyes around again and asked curiously:

"What's a wife? How come I didn't have one before?"

Rufeng: "It's a marriage bestowed by the Emperor. A wife is the person who will accompany you through wind and rain until old age."

Mo Chen smiled happily, "So that means Older Sister is going to play with me all the time from now on?"

Rufeng said:

"The Young Madam is frail and cannot speak, so she cannot be played with like a puppet in the military camp..."

At this, Rufeng cast a guilty glance at Ye Li, wondering if the Young Madam would still care now that she'd seen the general's current state...

After all, women all admire strength, and the general had previously been incomparably heroic and martial.

But now...

Mo Chen suddenly let out an exclamation of surprise and clapped his hands happily, looking completely like a child who had just received a beloved toy.

"I get to play with my older sister-wife from now on!"

Ye Li looked at the person before her. The contrast was so extreme that she felt a wee bit unadapted.

Is... is this the previously wise General Lord?

Strategic and resourceful?

A young hero?

She couldn't tell at all!!!!!!!!

Look at those starlight-bright eyes!

Look at the smiling face exposed by those eight pearly white teeth!

It blinded my precious designer eyes!

Help, is this still the general who stood above ten thousand people and below only one?

Mo Chen looked at the congee in her hands, his eyes lighting up as he said pitifully:

"I'm so hungry, Wife, can I eat?"

Ye Li snapped back to reality, nodded, and hurried forward.

Because he was weak from the fever, Ye Li stepped up to feed him the congee herself.

Mo Chen was starving indeed and ate quietly.

With every spoonful Ye Li offered, he swallowed it down, acting utterly well-behaved.

After finishing the bowl, just as Ye Li was about to put it down, Mo Chen suddenly reached out and hugged her!

Having never experienced such intimacy, Ye Li froze instantly.

Mo Chen said with complete satisfaction right by her ear:

"Wife, your cooking is so good, and you smell so nice, and you're so gentle."

"I like you best!"

chapters.title: Sweet Love Words from the General
chapters.content:
Mo Chen: "Wife, I like you the most!"

Ahhhhh help, so sweet!

The little deer in her heart was already crashing around and bruising itself...

Mo Chen's innocent and straightforward confession, accompanied by a warm embrace filled with strong masculine hormones and a magnetic voice lingering in her ears, gave Ye Li a jolt of extreme contrast, feeling like a current passing through her.

Mo Chen rubbed his stomach: "May I have a little more to eat? I'm so hungry."

So Ye Li seized the opportunity and bolted out as if fleeing for her life.

She went to the kitchen and brought back another bowl.

Once Mo Chen was full, Rufeng brought over the medicine, trying to persuade the general, who had lost his reason, to drink it.

Yet Mo Chen now only wanted to cling to Ye Li.

In the end, it was Ye Li who coaxed him into drinking the medicine, and then coaxed him until he fell asleep...

Outside the bedchamber, in the gazebo.

Ye Li sat on a chair, feeling a bit nervous.

Earlier, Rufeng had gestured for her to come out once she had Mo Chen settled.

Now Rufeng was kneeling properly on the ground, paying her respect before recounting the whole story from beginning to end.

It turned out that Mo Chen had served in the military and defended against enemies, frequently facing assassination attempts. He had been poisoned once before with a poison called "Carefree." After being poisoned, one would lose their sanity and become like a seven or eight-year-old child.

At that time, after the general was poisoned, his memory regressed to between seven and eight years old, and he lost all his martial arts skills.

Rufeng and several other subordinates had also gone through unimaginable hardships to find the divine doctor of the age, Divine Divine Doctor Mu, and begged him in person to cure the general.

It was just that the antidote was hard to find at the time, with only a single Blood Spirit Grass existing in the world.

Now the general had been harmed by traitors once again, and Rufeng needed to go out once more to search for the antidote, leaving the General's Estate in a precarious state...

Understanding the whole story, Ye Li nodded, and using water, she wrote on the table:

"Go find the antidote, I am here."

At first, Rufeng had thought this wife would be terrified, disappointed, or even want to leave, especially since the general had become no different from a fool in this state.

Yet earlier, the wife had clearly been very patient. Ever since they met, she seemed to have been in this state of taking things as they came.

Rufeng bowed again:

"The general once instructed that if anything unexpected happened to the General's Estate, her life should be protected above all else, allowing you to leave."

"Now that I am leaving the General's Estate to search for the antidote, does the Madam need to find a quiet place to take temporary refuge?"

"The General's personal guards will protect the General."

Ye Li wrote again:

"Stay, take care of him."

When she first arrived, it was Mo Chen who protected her. Now, it was her turn to protect him.

Rufeng had not expected this mute woman to be so calm and brave.

The general had given her all his money back then merely as compensation for her being dragged into the political struggles through no fault of her own.

It wasn't really meant for her to stand on the same front line as the General's Estate and weather the storm together.

Yet her unhesitating attitude now filled Rufeng with deep respect.

"Madam need not worry. Although this place is not the General's Estate, others will not dare to act rashly either. We will send people to protect both the General and Madam."

After briefly explaining the affairs of the General's Estate, Rufeng withdrew.

Ye Li wanted to check on Mo Chen. When she walked to the bedside, she discovered that Mo Chen was not asleep at all!

He was opening his eyes and looking at her, his pitiful gaze as helpless as someone who had been abandoned...

Ye Li had never seen him look like this. Ever since she transmigrated, he had shown valor and kindness, but he had never shown weakness.

She sat down beside him, and unable to speak, she took Mo Chen's hand and wrote:

"Not resting?"

Mo Chen leaned toward her with affectionate attachment:

"I'm not used to sleeping in this bed. Being alone in a dark room is so scary..."

Ye Li thought about it, indeed, this wasn't his real home after all.

A child is attached to home, after all.

She patted Mo Chen's hand and pointed toward the desk, signaling that she was going to get brush and ink.

Ye Li figured that while she wasn't good at coaxing children, she was good at drawing.

Since Mo Chen was like a child now, drawing a children's picture book couldn't be better.

She drew a few patterns of kittens and puppies for Mo Chen.

Seeing that Mo Chen was interested, she started drawing a four-panel comic.

A single sheet of paper was divided into four panels, and with just a few strokes, small animals sprang to life on the paper, the setup, development, turn, and conclusion of the four panels connecting vividly and naturally.

She drew a lighthearted, comedic comic, which left Mo Chen beaming with smiles and full of enthusiasm, repeatedly exclaiming how amazing his wife was.

Ye Li wondered if her tutor from the Academy of Fine Arts would praise her if they knew she was popularizing comics in ancient times.

Mo Chen was weak, but his curiosity was strong, and he kept acting spoiled, pestering her to look at more.

Ye Li didn't have many short stories in mind, so she decided to draw the world-famous picture book The Little Prince.

From minimalist lines to a simple sketch of an elephant, and then to the rose on the planet, she quietly drew this fairy tale written for adults.

The story of the Little Prince was not complicated. The aviator-like Little Prince had a falling out with his little rose on his own planet, so he embarked on interplanetary travel alone.

He went to many, many places, met many people, and finally became good friends with a fox.

The fox taught him the meaning of love and responsibility, so the Little Prince left Earth and returned to his one-and-only rose.

Ye Li loved the moral of the story: what is truly essential is invisible to the eye.

It is only with the heart that one can see rightly.

Yet Mo Chen drew an analogy from the story:

"I like this story. Maybe there are five thousand identical flowers in the world, but only you are my one and only rose, and my wife is also my only wife."

The young man's brows and eyes were gentle, carrying shyness and sincerity as he looked straight at Ye Li.

In an instant, her heart accelerated like a blaring siren. This was the second time she had heard him say these words.

The first time, he was still lucid and had given all his family wealth to her.

The second time, he had lost his sanity, yet he still remained full of trust in her.

A wave of emotion surged from the bottom of her heart.

When she finally coaxed Mo Chen until he was sleepy, he curled up quietly on the bed to rest.

He reached his hand out from under the quilt and grasped the sleeve of his young wife's robe.

Fearing that his fever might return, Ye Li stayed by his side to keep watch.

The next day.

Waking up, Mo Chen was full of energy and exceptionally restless.

Running and jumping around everywhere, Ye Li spent a lot of time and effort just helping him get up and wash up.

Fortunately, she had been quite a homebody in her past life, so she had plenty of patience. After tidying up his appearance, she brought him to the kitchen.

Ye Li figured she needed to study recipes properly today so she could open a restaurant and make money in the future.

To prevent Mo Chen from acting up like he did in the morning, Ye Li specially found a chair and had Mo Chen sit down in it.

Then she skillfully started the fire, boiled water in the pot, and cooked.

During the days when Mo Chen was unconscious, she had already grown familiar with the routine of an ancient kitchen, and even improvised and improved it with ease.

At first, Mo Chen stayed seated out of sheer novelty.

But later, taking advantage of the moment Ye Li went to pick scallions, he tried to help out in a very serious manner.

Only, while tending the fire, he pulled the burning wood right out of the stove and waved it around in the air, filling the kitchen with smoke everywhere...

As soon as Ye Li came back, she was so angry she nearly passed out; she simply wanted to give this mischievous child a beating with a stick.

Alas, her height was lacking, so she could only pull his hand down, take the wooden stick away, and put it back into the stove.

Ye Li patted his shoulder, then put her hands on her hips, making a very angry expression. Seeing that Mo Chen didn't understand her meaning,

she had no choice but to grab his hand, give it a sharp smack, point at the stove, give it another sharp smack, and point at the stove again.

Speaking of which, this training method was one Ye Li used to use on cats and dogs in the past, whenever they did something wrong, Ye Li would stop them on the spot, tell them it was wrong, and administer appropriate corporal punishment.

That way, the cats at home had become very sensible.

Mo Chen was big and tall, watching the petite wife before him angrily patting the back of his hand, her eyes wide and round like a red rabbit's, her face full of rage.

He finally realized that his older sister-wife was unhappy, so he quickly apologized and said:

"I'm sorry, did I do something wrong? Does wife not like me? I'll be good, please don't be angry."

Looking at his expression that instantly fell, coupled with that childish tone and his submissive, low-pitched plea for forgiveness,

and recalling his image as a general who didn't change his expression even when shot by arrows and persecuted by the emperor, her heart instantly softened.

Sigh...

When all was said and done, he was poisoned, and he still had injuries on his body...

If he were still in his right mind, he certainly wouldn't act up like this or apologize.

Comforting herself while letting out a resigned sigh of fate,

Ye Li pointed at the chair. This time, Mo Chen finally understood her meaning.

"You want me to sit over there, right?" He sat obediently in the chair, not moving an inch.

Now Ye Li finally had some free time. She tidied up the stove and cooked some simple home-style dishes, making pan-fried buns and sweet potato cakes for dessert, figuring a child would probably like to eat them.

The rich and savory aroma drifted through the kitchen, whetting one's appetite. She turned around, full of joy, wanting to let Mo Chen have the first bite.

Never expected that the moment she turned her head, she would be so startled that her soul almost ascended to heaven!

Mo Chen was actually hanging himself with a white silk sash!

Ye Li tried to stop him, but accidentally bumped into the table...

Anxiously, she raised her eyes to look, just as Mo Chen was about to bring his neck close to the tied noose...

She wanted to cry out to stop him, only to remember that this original body was mute...

chapters.title: I'll Sell Milk Tea to Support You
chapters.content:
The moment Ye Li turned around, she saw Mo Chen hanging himself!

The tall and imposing General was standing on a stool, looking utterly distraught.

He was holding a white veil and tying a knot, his head already reaching forward to slip into it. She was so terrified that she dropped her chopsticks!

She lunged forward in a flash, grabbing Mo Chen by the thigh in an attempt to pull him down.

Unbeknownst to her, she was moving too fast in her panic and couldn't stop, so she crashed straight into Mo Chen, sending them both tumbling to the floor.

Amidst the chaos, numerous pots, pans, bowls, and dishes were knocked over, a clattering and crashing chorus echoing through the kitchen.

A small half-basin of flour on the edge of the table was also kicked over, sending a cloud of white dust billowing into the air.

The white veil on the rafters was pulled down in the scuffle, fluttering in the wind and draping gracefully over them.

Ye Li, enveloped in the white veil, landed squarely on top of Mo Chen.

When they fell just now, Mo Chen had used his instincts to shield Ye Li.

Ye Li wasn't hurt much, but Mo Chen's back hit the ground directly, and he let out a muffled groan.

Ye Li propped herself up, wanting to check on Mo Chen. Just as the white veil draped over her face, she had to lift the veil to look at him from underneath the gauze...

At this moment, their spot happened to be bathed in sunlight, and the warm, pleasant light shone down on Ye Li, who was covered in the white veil. It looked like a holy halo, and the floating flour looked like snowflakes, making her hazy and ethereal.

Like a divine being.

Mo Chen looked at Ye Li like this and was completely dazed.

His heart suddenly began to beat rapidly, as if he were sick. He only felt that the person before him was radiating a holy light, so dazzling that he couldn't look away...

Over on her side, Ye Li was pale with fright. Watching Mo Chen fall, she couldn't speak and couldn't even ask questions.

She could only gently grope around his body, carefully checking him to see if he was injured anywhere else.

A moment later, Mo Chen suddenly hugged Ye Li tightly and sobbed:

"Wuwuwuwu... Am I completely useless? No one likes me."

"Mom and Dad are gone, and Big Sister doesn't like me either, she doesn't want to play with me. I'm the most useless person in this world... Wuwuwu, I don't deserve to live..."

Ye Li hadn't expected that the current Mo Chen not only had his age reverted, but was also stuck in the most vulnerable stage of childhood.

Family separated and lost, lonely and helpless.

He wasn't even used to sleeping in unfamiliar beds, let alone all of this strangeness.

She began to reflect on the fact that she hadn't considered things from his perspective.

Ye Li calmed her emotions and slowly reached out to stroke Mo Chen's head, stroke by stroke, with great patience.

Mo Chen kept crying, holding onto her body.

Clinging to her tightly in bewilderment and helplessness, afraid that she would run away.

Ye Li's heart ached.

She thought: Perhaps she was wrong.

Whether a General or a young master, everyone grows from a child into an adult.

Being able to smile while recounting the past doesn't mean it wasn't painful at the time.

What she had always seen was a calm and composed Mo Chen, but how could someone like that simply be born that way?

Turns out he was like this when he was little too, crying, laughing, and making a fuss just like a normal person...

Ye Li began to understand Mo Chen, and her heart ached for someone who had lost his parents and fought single-handedly to protect his country.

Embracing each other, time passed very slowly in this moment.

Mo Chen's crying gradually grew softer.

The hand comforting his head had been so gentle the whole time...

It pressed against his heart like a feather. Her hand was warm and soft, patting him gently and firmly, stroke by stroke.

Mo Chen didn't know what this feeling was, but instinctively he yearned for this moment to last forever, yearning for this gentle person to always stay by his side.

The sunlight spilled over them, and the two figures covered by the white veil faintly radiated a soft glow.

Specks of starlight drifted in the air; that was the luster of the flour reflecting the sunlight.

The warm tones blended softly into the atmosphere of the moment, tranquil and cozy, like a picture scroll frozen in time.

When Rufeng followed the aroma of the dishes in, this was the exact scene that met his eyes:

The General and the Young Madam were locked in a tight embrace, bathed in the sunlight, with the white veil draped over them, looking so ethereal it was as if they were glowing...

"Ahem, Young Master, Young Madam..." Rufeng greeted the General awkwardly.

Rufeng truly hadn't expected the relationship between the General and the Young Madam to progress this fast!

At first, he had been worried that the General would lose his memory and revert to a child's mentality, which would damage his dignity. But looking at the two of them acting like glue now...

It seemed the Young Madam had still fallen for the General's charm; as expected of the husband adored by thousands of maidens in the capital.

Our Lord General is simply the most formidable no matter when!

Awesome!

"This Young Madam is a lady, the ground is cold, these things are better handled back in the main courtyard..."

Hearing Rufeng's voice, Ye Li was utterly dumbfounded on the spot.

When did Rufeng get here?

What does he mean by saying that?

Nothing happened between us at all!

Help me ah ah ah ah ah!!!!!!

We're being misunderstood again, again, and again!

With a crying tone, Mo Chen whimpered intermittently to Rufeng:

"Big Sister doesn't like me, she doesn't want to say a single word to me, I'm not likable at all, wuwuwuwu..."

Ye Li felt her head ache listening to this...

Rufeng hurriedly stepped forward to explain, "Young Master, the Young Madam is feeling unwell and cannot speak right now, but she definitely doesn't hate you."

Rufeng looked up at Ye Li, "Right, Young Madam?"

I, who have never missed a chance to play my part in the script you need.

Ye Li took the cue and smiled at Mo Chen.

She pointed at her throat with her finger, crossed her hands to make an "X" shape, and told him she couldn't speak.

Mo Chen came to a sudden realization: "So Big Sister Wife wasn't ignoring me, it's because she hurt her throat and can't speak!"

Rufeng explained, "Young Master, the Young Madam's given name is Ye Li."

Mo Chen finished listening and said, "Ye Li? Ye Li... Hahaha, I like pears too, I like Big Sister's name, and I like you!"

Another unprovoked confession out of nowhere.

Ye Li indicated that she was now a person who had seen big scenes; stay calm...

Stay calm.

She continued to project a friendly smile, hoping this unruly child who had just finished throwing a suicide tantrum wouldn't go off misunderstanding things on his own again.

Rufeng smoothed things over just in time:

"The Young Madam's culinary skills are peerless. Young Master, get up first and let's go have our meal."

"Yay, yay, I want to eat food made by Pear Wife!"

What kind of magical nickname is this?!

Lord General, can your antidote be shipped via SF Express?

"So, Pear Wife, you don't hate me, do you?"

Mo Chen asked her nervously for confirmation, his expression cautious, like a child who had done something wrong waiting for judgment.

Ye Li told herself helplessly: Practice makes perfect.

So she shook her head to indicate she didn't hate him, and at the same time returned the matching eight-toothed broad smile so Mo Chen could directly feel her sincerity.

"Then are you willing to play with me?"

Smile, nod, "I am willing."

Mo Chen frowned, looking a bit sad as he said:

"But I don't know how to do anything, I'm afraid I won't be a good husband."

Ye Li wrote on the table: "It's fine, I'll sell milk tea to support you."

"What is milk tea?"

Ye Li wrote: "A delicious drink, you'll like it."

I ask you, what child doesn't like milk tea?

Mo Chen's sword-like brows suddenly furrowed, as if feeling uncertain:

"Pear Wife, are you really doing this of your own free will?"

Why does this kid have so many questions?

If Ye Li could speak at this moment, she probably could have been heard roaring all over the courtyard:

I! AM! WILLING!

I wouldn't leave you even if a dung beetle left its dung, okay?

Please, no more self-abusive hanging performances...

...

Dying of laughter is probably a matter of these next few days.

Ye Li thought with a smile.

After clearing up the misunderstanding, when the few of them sat down to eat again, it was almost noon.

The dishes Ye Li made today were all home-style plates: Mapo Tofu, stir-fried shredded radish with potato and pork slices, steamed fish with shredded ginger and scallions, and stir-fried greens with minced pork. Although they looked ordinary, each dish was infused with plenty of seasonings and spices, making them much more fragrant than usual dishes.

Just as Mo Chen was about to eat, a servant suddenly rushed in to report:

"The Emperor has bestowed a grand reward upon the General. The General is to enter the palace later to express his gratitude."

Rufeng exclaimed in shock, "What?!"

Ye Li inwardly shouted bad news!

She thought to herself, with Mo Chen having lost his wits right now, wouldn't entering the palace be a death sentence?

Rufeng looked at Ye Li, "This is bad, we need to think of something."

Mo Chen, who was eating with utter cuteness, saw his wife looking at him, flashed a bright eight-toothed grin, and beamed with joy.

Looking at his innocent smile, Ye Li made up her mind:

He absolutely cannot enter the palace!

chapters.title: For Your Sake, Burning the Imperial Residence and Escaping Alive
chapters.content:
Mo Chen did not realize the severity of the situation.

However, Rufeng had already anxiously grabbed Mo Chen’s hand and said to Ye Li:

"Pardon my offense, Madam, please come with me. The General must not enter the palace now, let’s escape first!"

Ye Li dipped her finger in clean water and wrote on the table:

"Escape where? He is the General."

Unless a general is away from home, the sovereign's orders need not be obeyed.

Otherwise, here in the capital city, there was no escaping it.

Rufeng could not care about that anymore. He dropped to his knees and said:

"Even if I die, I will carve out a bloody path for the General and Madam, allowing you to leave the capital safely. Then the General's personal guards will find a doctor to cure the poison!"

Seeing Rufeng so anxious, Mo Chen also began to realize the seriousness of the situation:

"Is someone going to kill me? We have to escape? Can we not go home anymore?"

Ye Li looked at him. He wanted to go home.

In that case, the only course of action now was...

The young man's eyes were bewildered and helpless. Then he looked at Rufeng and finally made up his mind:

"I listen to Brother Rufeng, but you must come with us too. I don't want you to be in danger."

"Young Master, no. I must stay behind to hold the rear."

Ye Li tapped on the table, interrupting the deeply affectionate master and servant.

Then she wrote a line of characters on the table.

Rufeng looked at it and was greatly shocked: "This..."

Ye Li wrote: "Do as I say."

Having watched so many palace intrigue dramas, there were still ways to avoid entering the palace.

Rufeng acknowledged the order.

There was no better way at present!

Ye Li and Mo Chen ate their fill leisurely before going out to receive the imperial decree.

The leading palace eunuch originally wanted to seize the opportunity to make trouble.

But just as he was about to speak, a sudden change occurred!

Assassins launched an attack just as the General and Madam were about to receive the decree!

Arrows tipped with flames suddenly shot right to his feet!

Following that, countless fire arrows came raining down. Their targets were Mo Chen and Ye Li.

However, the palace servants and eunuchs who came to read the decree were also listed as targets, shot indiscriminately...

Those arrows not only carried fire, but also accelerants like oil.

After being shot inside, they directly ignited the curtains, fabrics, and various wooden materials in the room.

For a moment, the scene fell into chaos.

Mo Chen hurriedly took Ye Li to escape, the two of them stumbling forward, trying to avoid the flames.

Those arrows could be seen following them and shooting all the way.

The arrowheads carried fire, and as they fled all the way, the entire bestowed residence was surrounded by fire arrows along the way.

In an instant, it became a sea of fire, and the large bestowed residence suddenly turned into a trapped beast's burning cage.

The palace servants and eunuchs were trapped within, crying out in despair and begging for help.

Ye Li hurried back to the room to grab a quilt, then ran to the pond to drench all the quilts in water before covering her and Mo Chen's heads with them.

She and Mo Chen escaped to the edge of the fire, and then Ye Li picked up a wooden board and pressed it against a large stone, making a simple lever.

Afterwards, she hung a silk cloth outside the courtyard wall and told Mo Chen that when the lever bounced up later, he should use the momentum to jump out.

However, young Mo Chen was too young and refused to go first; he wanted Ye Li to escape first.

Ye Li went up first, and Mo Chen followed closely behind, but the lever was temporarily constructed after all, and its direction could not be controlled.

In the end, by the time the two of them landed, they were already injured.

The raging fire burned fiercely, and a little eunuch screamed at the top of his lungs:

"Fire! There's a fire! Put out the fire quickly, put it out!"

Because it was an imperial-bestowed residence, the estate was very large. The sudden glare of the fire attracted people all over the capital to look over, and many people joined the ranks of firefighting.

Amidst the sky-full of firelight, Ye Li felt as if her own peaceful life had also been burned to ashes.

From now on, there would be treacherous and unpredictable court struggles.

Since just a moment ago, Mo Chen had been choked by the smoke and seemed uncomfortable, coughing incessantly and panting.

Yet he forcefully held it back. Seeing him suppress his painful breathing, Ye Li gently massaged his chest.

Mo Chen's eyes slowly opened, his deep phoenix eyes looking at Ye Li. Having survived a disaster, he smiled and said:

"It's so good that I can still be with my wife."

For some reason, Ye Li felt that amidst the sky-full of firelight, his gaze was somewhat tender.

This newly bestowed residence could not be used at the moment. No matter how hard one tried to put out the fire, ancient wooden houses would burn down in a large swath once ignited.

Ye Li said to Mo Chen: "Let's go home."

Mo Chen held out his hand to Ye Li: "Okay, let's go home."

Ye Li stared fixedly at the hand before her. There were thick calluses on his hand, as well as scars.

Yet this hand, clearly resolute and powerful, appeared so gentle.

Ye Li placed her hand in his palm, letting him lead her away.

The sky-full of firelight roared and burned behind them, as if trying to burn away all filth, while she quietly followed him toward the front, as if as long as she followed him, the danger behind them was insignificant.

Ye Li thought to herself, although she had encountered many, many things after transmigrating, it had always been safe and sound. Since she had no cheat code (golden finger), she might as well cling to a powerful supporter.

If the mountain will not come to me, I will go to the mountain.

At this moment, Rufeng led the personal guards over and immediately brought the injured General and Madam back to the General's Mansion.

Within days, this matter spread throughout the capital, becoming the newest topic of conversation over tea and biscuits!

Tianhuo Country's bravest General was assassinated in broad daylight on the streets of the capital, and then his imperial-bestowed residence was burned down by assassins once again!

For a time, everyone was cursing the assassin for being too arrogant, and cursing the capital's guards for their incompetence...

Even the General's life was hanging by a thread, wouldn't everyone else's lives be in jeopardy?

Daring to burn down a residence bestowed by the Emperor was trampling the Son of Heaven's majesty underfoot!

For a time, public grievances filled the streets among the common people, who successively demanded the assassins be found and the vicious criminals severely punished!

On the other hand, there were new rumors.

That was, the General's Madam had been seriously injured while protecting the General and blocking arrows for him.

The General was extremely worried, and therefore took the General's Madam back to the General's Mansion, closed the doors to guests, and was even too busy to attend court, wanting to personally treat his Madam's injuries.

For a time, the people of the capital praised General Mo Chen for being affectionate, righteous, and a man of true character.

As for the Emperor, he was so angry in the palace that he smashed a floor full of porcelain. Someone actually dared to hold imperial majesty in such contempt, killing Mo Chen was one thing, but daring to burn down the imperial residence as well! He issued an order to thoroughly investigate this matter!

As for Mo Chen entering the palace to express his gratitude, it had long been forgotten by everyone...

The General's Mansion.The Main Courtyard.

At this moment, Ye Li's face was flushed and her heart was beating wildly. She had no idea how things had turned out like this!

Why was she lying in bed with Mo Chen again, and being held like a mascot?

The young man opposite her had a pair of clear and moving dark pupils, looking at her with unspoken feelings as he murmured:

"What is today's bedtime story?"

They had just barely escaped death, why did they still need to listen to a story?

Child, wouldn't it be better for you to go to sleep early?

Please stop acting cute with that face all the time!

Ye Li was speechless and choked with no words, silently recalling what happened an hour ago...

At that time, they had left the sea of fire, and Rufeng had driven the carriage to the General's Mansion.

Because of the assassin's twist of events, the wind direction in the entire capital instantly reversed. General Mo Chen had been trapped in the sea of fire at the bestowed residence, and thus brought his wife back to the estate.

Lifting the curtain and looking at the home where Mo Chen grew up, it was indeed somewhat rustic and shabby.

The dark gray building before her eyes, everything appeared so old and time-worn.

Only the inscribed characters on the plaque were powerful and vigorous, reminding people of the estate's former glory, yet it seemed as though no one had lived there for a long time, unable to conceal the desolation.

Mo Chen had not spoken a word since getting into the sedan chair. Only upon seeing the General's Mansion did he smile, and he cautiously said:

"Wife, we're home."

Mo Chen was even more excited than before. He took Ye Li's hand and led her in through the main gate.

After entering the mansion, Rufeng said to Ye Li admiringly:

"Madam is truly bold and resolute; you actually thought of this method!"

"Now we have returned smoothly, and it won't arouse suspicion."

Mo Chen also applauded from the side: "Wife is amazing!"

Ye Li smiled sheepishly.

As it turned out, given the critical situation at the time, Ye Li had asked Rufeng to find people to pretend to be assassins and shoot arrows once more.

Burn the imperial residence, and then spread the news in the capital.

In this way, they logically avoided the decree to enter the palace and were able to return to the General's Mansion.

That was why Rufeng held Ye Li's boldness and resolution in such high esteem, an imperial bestowal, and she said burn it and burn it she did.

No one had ever dared to do such a thing; others lacked the courage, and the master who received the bestowal would certainly not bear to part with it.

However, having transmigrated, Ye Li had no particular affection for this emperor's reward; if it was burned, it was burned.

Therefore, no one would suspect that Ye Li had people burn down the residence the Emperor had given her for her marriage.

Remembering that the Madam did this for the General's sake, Rufeng bowed deeply and respectfully to her:

"Previously, I underestimated Madam's breadth of mind and strategic skill. If the General recovers his wits, he will surely praise Madam's heroic martial spirit this time!"

"Madam and the General are truly a match made in heaven, a heaven-sent union!"

While kneeling, Rufeng offered flattery.

Scaring Ye Li into hurriedly helping him up.

Rufeng now held the utmost reverence for Ye Li and asked:

"Since we have returned, where would Madam like to reside?"

Mo Chen directly stated: "Live with me! Live with me!"

Then, on his own accord, he took Ye Li's hand and ran towards the main courtyard of the General's Mansion...

The moment they stepped through the door, Mo Chen pinned Ye Li against the door, wrapping his entire body around her as he said with boundless joy:

"I've finally brought my wife home!"

"Brother Rufeng said we are a match made in heaven and a heaven-sent union. I'm so happy!"
